verdict: Snap-on sales dipped 1% as diesel-price turbulence hit its van channel, but a record quarter in critical industries and firm gross margins kept profit at $243M.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: total revenue $1,282M vs $1,292M a year ago

kpis.label: Capital spending
kpis.note: money spent on buildings and equipment in the quarter; ~$100M planned for 2026

segments.name: Commercial & Industrial Group
segments.note: Tools and equipment for critical industries such as aerospace, military and energy — a record quarter, up 10% with help from acquisitions.

segments.name: Snap-on Tools Group
segments.note: Sales through franchisee vans to vehicle technicians — down 7% as high diesel prices led franchisees to cut inventories.

segments.name: Repair Systems & Information Group
segments.note: Diagnostics, repair information and shop equipment — down 2% on weaker activity with car dealerships, partly offset by acquisitions.

segments.name: Financial Services
segments.note: Interest and fees from financing tools and franchise operations — roughly flat at $99M.

segments.name: Intersegment eliminations
segments.note: Sales between Snap-on's own groups, removed so revenue is not double-counted.

opex.name: Operating expenses
opex.note: Day-to-day running costs of the tools, equipment and information businesses.

opex.name: Financial services expenses
opex.note: Cost of running the financing arm that lends to franchisees and technicians.

takeaways.title: The van channel stumbled
takeaways.text: Snap-on Tools Group sales fell 7% to $471M. The company blames an unusually sharp rise in diesel prices, which pushed franchisees to trim inventories even though demand from technicians stayed stable.

takeaways.title: Critical industries set a record
takeaways.text: Commercial & Industrial sales rose 10% to $404M, with operating earnings up 30% to $75M, led by aerospace, military and precision-torque work.

takeaways.title: Margins held firm
takeaways.text: Gross profit was $604M on product sales — about 51% of net sales — showing pricing and cost discipline even as volumes softened. The year-ago quarter also included a $22M legal-settlement benefit that did not repeat.

otherDetail: Other income of $3M is $15M of other income minus $13M (rounded) of interest expense.
footerNote: Consolidated net earnings were $250M; $7M belonged to noncontrolling interests, leaving $243M attributable to Snap-on shareholders.
